question: Why does the Beets lane reproduce badly (31.3% spread at n=3) while Fastify reproduces to 1.7%?

inputs.per_task_method: Codex reports cumulative thread totals; a task's cost is its final usage snapshot minus the previous task's.

finding: Beets does not vary because one task is unstable. Per-task variability is comparable in both lanes; what differs is whether it cancels. In Fastify the per-task deviations offset (cancellation ratio 12.4x) and no replicate is consistently dear. In Beets they align (ratio 1.1x): one replicate is the most expensive in 6 of 7 tasks and another the cheapest in 6 of 7, so deviations compound instead of averaging out.
mechanism: The workflow is one persistent session, so context accumulates across tasks and roughly two thirds of weighted cost is cached input. A session that pulls in more context early carries that penalty into every later task. Fastify re-converges -- its cheapest first task, r2 at 87,056 against 152,573, still ends with the largest final context -- so early exploration is traded against later exploration and final context lands within 5%. Beets never re-converges: final context spreads 40%.
not_supported: Cache warming across runs: the cached share of input is flat at 95.5-97.3% across all six sessions.
A single pathological task: the spread is distributed, with task-07 contributing 35%, task-05 21% and task-06 20%.
Task file overlap: both lanes change exactly one distinct production file per task.
consequence: At three replicates the Beets lane cannot resolve a treatment effect below roughly 30%. Fastify at 1.7% can resolve far smaller effects. Adding Beets replicates narrows the median but does not remove the compounding, because the correlation is within a session rather than between sessions. Selecting low-variance tasks is not a usable lever: Beets task-04 is quiet but is followed by tasks spreading 36%, 36% and 60%, and in a persistent session a later task inherits whatever divergence preceded it.

per_task_ranking.note: Beets task-04 is the lowest-variance task in either lane at 3.5%, so it is not true that every Beets task is unstable. Its low increment is partly offsetting rather than intrinsic: at that point the replicates' carried context differed 22.5% while their step counts differed 18.2% in the opposite direction (11, 11, 13), so the two nearly cancel within the task.

convergence.finding: Both lanes diverge immediately and only one recovers. Cumulative carried context is already 88.3% apart after Fastify task-01 and 44.4% apart after Beets task-01. Fastify then closes: 31.6%, 16.3%, 7.8%, 6.6%, 4.9% by the final task. Beets does not: 28.8%, 31.4%, 22.5%, 28.6%, 32.8%, 39.6%. The distinguishing property is convergence of accumulated context, not per-task stability.

rebuild_test.change: Beets rebuilt from 7 independent beetsplug modules to 6 tasks in the beets/ core package (2026-08-20).
rebuild_test.prediction_registered_before_r1: If front-loading is what makes a lane converge, the rebuilt lane should still reproduce badly, near 31.3% rather than Fastify's 1.7%.
rebuild_test.conclusion: Sharing a code region is not the lever. The rebuilt lane is materially cheaper -- 573,627 and 713,166 against 862,731 to 977,781 for the plugin set -- but no less variable, and it front-loads less than the set it replaced. Task selection therefore does not explain the difference between the lanes. Fastify's convergence remains unexplained and is the thing to investigate; the remaining candidates are the persistent-session design itself, the intrinsic open-endedness of the Beets tasks, and repository or language differences that the two-lane contrast cannot separate.
rebuild_test.cost_note: A cheaper lane that is equally noisy is not progress: resolving a treatment effect depends on spread, not on the total.

prompt_openness_test.question: Is the Beets variance caused by prompts that leave too much open?
prompt_openness_test.measure: spread in fresh input tokens for the same task across replicates, i.e. how differently the agent explores when given the same prompt
prompt_openness_test.finding: Partly yes, and only for the rebuilt lane. Two of its six prompts drive runaway exploration: beets-migration-text-paths-v2 at 211.6% and beets-subcommand-help-alignment-v2 at 101.7%, against a worst case of 82% in Fastify and 62% in the archived plugin lane. Both prompts were written by hand for the rebuild rather than carried over.

defects_identified.defect: The title, 'Keep a short subcommand's description on its own line', is ambiguous and reads naturally as the opposite of the intent. The body and completion condition require the description to stay on the same line as the name; 'its own line' invites the reading that the description belongs on a separate line, which is the seeded bug.

Bundles two independent requirements -- skip rows with no stored path, and convert text path values -- and describes a rarely exercised administrative code path, so locating it costs more search and the cost varies with how the search happens to go.

prompt_openness_test.does_not_explain_everything: The archived plugin lane spread 31.3% with no runaway task at all, its worst being 62%. So prompt openness cannot be the whole cause: that lane's variance was distributed rather than concentrated. There are two distinct sources -- a structural one visible without any runaway task, and a prompt-driven one introduced by the rebuild.
prompt_openness_test.recommendation: Repair the two prompts and re-baseline before drawing further conclusions about the lane. That is cheap relative to a treatment campaign and isolates the prompt-driven component. It will not by itself reach Fastify's 1.7%, because the structural component remains.

prompt_repair_result_20260821.change: Six prompts rewritten 2026-08-21; both lanes requalified and re-baselined at n=2.
prompt_repair_result_20260821.finding: Mixed and not conclusive at n=2. The two prompts with the largest exploration gaps improved sharply -- migration-text-paths 212% to 62% and subcommand-help-alignment 102% to 15% -- which is the predicted direction. But cached-attribute-error-surface was also repaired and got worse, 30% to 135%, and concurrent-plugin-dispatch, the untouched exemplar, went 21% to 69%. A prompt that was not edited moving that far means single-pair gaps are dominated by run-to-run noise, so the improvements cannot be separated from it.
prompt_repair_result_20260821.direction_change: The one qualitative shift: pre-repair all six Beets tasks moved the same way between replicates, so deviations accumulated and a 24.8% per-task median passed through to a 24.3% lane total. Post-repair the signs alternate (+-+-+-) and the lane total, 16.4%, falls below several individual task gaps. Some cancellation is now present. Whether that is a property of the repaired tasks or a coincidence of two runs is untested.
prompt_repair_result_20260821.not_established: That the repair reduced variance. Fastify, which also had two prompts repaired, moved from 0.45% to 4.0%. Neither lane has enough replicates to estimate a spread rather than observe one gap.

n3_verdict.finding: The repair did not fix the lane. At three replicates the repaired Beets lane spreads 22.2%, against 24.3% at n=2 pre-repair and 31.3% for the plugin set, and its cancellation ratio is 1.4x against 1.1x for the plugin set and 12.4x for Fastify. Deviations still accumulate rather than offset. The alternating signs observed at n=2 did not survive the third replicate.
n3_verdict.prompt_precision_verdict: Not supported as a lever on lane variance. Exploration gaps at n=3 are 42-135% across all six tasks, including 69% for concurrent-plugin-dispatch, which was never edited and whose 0.2% pair was the entire basis for the design principles. That 0.2% was a fortunate draw, not a property. The four principles remain a reasonable style guide and are not evidence-backed as a variance control.
n3_verdict.what_is_established: Lane variance is governed by whether per-task deviations cancel, not by their size. Fastify cancels at 12.4x and reproduces to 1.7%; both Beets task sets fail to cancel, at 1.1x and 1.4x, and reproduce to 22-31% despite comparable per-task magnitudes. Three interventions have now failed to induce cancellation in Beets: shared code region, task count matched to Fastify, and prompt precision.
n3_verdict.recommended_next: Stop modifying Beets tasks. The remaining untested difference is structural -- the persistent session and how context accumulates within it -- and it is testable directly by resetting context between tasks on one lane and comparing, rather than by further task authoring.

correction_to_earlier_reporting: The n=3 repaired spread (22.2%) was compared against an n=2 pre-repair spread (24.3%). Spread grows with sample size, so that comparison understated the repair. At matched n=2 the lane went 24.3% to 16.4%, a 33% relative reduction, and at matched n=3 the plugin set to the repaired core set went 31.3% to 22.2%. The direction is consistent in both.

zero-penalty-display was described as the lane's worst task on a 54% weighted range. That range is confounded by position: it runs last and inherits all accumulated context, so its weighted cost is the largest of the six for reasons unrelated to the task. On the position-independent measure it is the tightest task in the lane.
seed_size_finding_20260821.finding: Seed size predicts exploration gap. Across the six repaired Beets tasks at n=3 the rank correlation between seed patch size and between-replicate fresh-token gap is +1.00: 420 chars to 42%, 637 to 44%, 942 to 62%, 1,217 to 62%, 1,259 to 69%, 2,701 to 135%.
seed_size_finding_20260821.why_fastify_shows_no_correlation: Its seeds span 520 to 855 characters, a 1.6x range, against 6.4x for Beets. There is too little variation to detect a slope, and the whole Fastify range sits below the point where Beets degrades.
seed_size_finding_20260821.proposed_guideline: Cap seed size at roughly 900 characters, the top of Fastify's range. On the current Beets set that would exclude cached-attribute-error-surface at 2,701, concurrent-plugin-dispatch at 1,259 and migration-text-paths at 1,217, and retain the two tightest. This is a mechanical, checkable property of a candidate, unlike the four prose principles it replaces.
seed_size_finding_20260821.limits: Six tasks at three replicates. The correlation is with seed size, which plausibly proxies for how bounded the underlying defect is rather than causing anything by itself. It addresses per-task exploration only and says nothing about cancellation, which is the lane-level property that governs the total.

repin_result_20260822.lane: Beets repinned to 746cecf2, six tasks with seeds 468-794 chars
repin_result_20260822.finding: Best Beets pair so far at 8.8%, against 13.3%, 24.3% and 16.4% for the three previous task sets at the same sample size. Exploration gaps also fell: four of six tasks are at or below 13% where the previous set's best was 42%. That is the direction the seed-size bound predicted.
repin_result_20260822.caveat: Cancellation did not appear. The ratio is 1.5x against 1.1-1.4x for the earlier Beets sets and 12.4x for Fastify, and five of six deviations still point the same way. The lane improved by making per-task deviations smaller, not by making them offset, so the mechanism that distinguishes Fastify remains absent and unexplained.
repin_result_20260822.status: one pair; not a spread estimate. A third replicate is what would separate this from a lucky draw.
